note: Glossary shown on data.html (client page). Edit here; the page fetches this file. Keep it plain-language, one sentence of 'what it is' and one of 'how we use it'.

sections.title: Commodity prices
sections.intro: The carousel on the home page and the Market tab. Assessments are published prices from the named agency; futures/exchange prices are live.

items.desc: Platts' daily assessment of 61% Fe iron ore fines delivered to China (CFR Qingdao). Reference for Vale's and CSN Mineração's realised prices; the home carousel and the Steel & Mining prices tab use it.
The 62% Fe benchmark used by the market at large. On the Market tab it is the driver line behind VALE3 and CMIN3; the SGX contract (FEF) is the exchange-traded version.
High- and low-grade assessments. The spread between them is the market's price for quality — relevant to Vale's premium products.

items.term: Brand assessments (Pilbara Blend, Brazilian Blend, Newman, MAC, Jimblebar)
items.desc: Prices of specific ore brands. Brazilian Blend Fines (BRBF) is Vale's flagship product; the others are the main Australian brands it competes with.
Premium paid for direct-reduction/blast-furnace pellets over fines. A direct input to Vale's and CSN's pellet revenue.
Capesize freight rates on the two main iron ore routes. The Brazil route is roughly three times the Australian one, which is why freight matters more for Brazilian miners' netbacks.
Swap prices for future quarters of the 62% Fe index. A downward-sloping curve (backwardation) means the market expects prices to fall.
Hot-rolled coil export price from China. The reference for import parity into Brazil and the main driver for CSN, Usiminas and Gerdau's flat steel pricing.
Turkish rebar export price, the global benchmark for long steel. Relevant for Gerdau's long-steel businesses.

items.term: Hard coking coal (HCC FOB Australia, Premium / Low Vol)
items.desc: Metallurgical coal for blast furnaces. Brazil imports essentially all of its coking coal, so this is a cash-cost line for the integrated steelmakers.
Bleached hardwood kraft pulp (eucalyptus) delivered to China, net of discounts. The single most important price for Suzano and a key one for Klabin and CMPC.
Bleached softwood kraft pulp delivered to China. The BHKP–NBSK spread signals substitution pressure between the two fibres.
Domestic Chinese resale price, converted by us from yuan to dollars: (yuan ÷ 1.13 VAT − 150) ÷ FX. A resale price below the net import price means the spot market is softer than the list price.
European pulp prices. Europe is the second market for Brazilian pulp and usually prices at a premium to China.
Front-month COMEX copper. Driver for Southern Copper, Grupo México and the Aura copper mines.
Front-month COMEX gold. The main driver for Aura Minerals.
LME nickel cash price, used in the morning blast. Relevant to Vale Base Metals.
Oil and aluminium references used in the morning blast and in cost discussions (fuel, energy).

sections.title: Steel & Mining data
sections.intro: The Steel & Mining dashboard (Prices, Domestic Market, Imports, Exports). Everything is monthly official data; the underlying tables can be downloaded with the ⤓ Data button.

items.desc: Brazilian steel imports by product and country of origin from customs declarations. Price = customs value ÷ volume.
Brazilian steel exports by product and destination. The export price is used as a proxy for the domestic reference price.
Import price minus the domestic reference. Positive = imports are more expensive than domestic steel (protective); negative = domestic prices under pressure.

items.source: IBBA model on SECEX (55 anti-dumping products)
items.desc: Our estimate of Brazilian imports of the 55 steel products subject to anti-dumping, from Korea and China, on the same tariff lines as the official series.
What Korea and China report as steel shipped to Brazil. Ships take ~45 days, so this series anticipates the SECEX import line.

items.term: Crude steel production / domestic sales / apparent consumption
items.desc: The Brazil Steel Institute's monthly performance report. Apparent consumption = domestic sales + imports; import penetration = imports ÷ apparent consumption.
Flat steel distributors' stock and flows. Inventory in months = stock ÷ average monthly sales; a leading read on restocking cycles.
Brazilian iron ore fines and pellet exports by destination country.
The same month across several years, side by side. Useful to separate a seasonal dip from a real change in demand.

sections.title: Pulp & Paper data
sections.intro: The Pulp & Paper dashboard (Pulp, Paper & Packaging). Monthly official and industry data.

items.term: Pulp export volume / revenue by port
items.desc: Brazilian pulp exports by port of shipment. Ports map roughly to producers (Santos → Suzano/Klabin, Vitória → Suzano, Paranaguá → Klabin/Arauco).
Export revenue ÷ volume. Lags the PIX price by roughly one to two months because of shipping and invoicing.
Monthly paper statistics by grade. Read by machine vision from the published PDF and checked against the totals printed in it.
Corrugated packaging shipments, the demand indicator for Klabin's and Irani's packaging businesses. Shipments per working day remove calendar effects.

items.source: General Administration of Customs of China
items.desc: Chinese imports of hardwood and softwood chips by origin (Vietnam, Australia, others). Chips are the fibre for Chinese integrated mills — a proxy for Chinese pulp production.
Sum of the last twelve months. Smooths seasonality and revisions.

sections.title: News Hunter
sections.intro: The news feed on the home page and the News Hunter tab.

items.desc: Our AI's reading of whether the headline is positive, negative or neutral for the covered companies — always from the covered companies' point of view (e.g., a fall in iron ore is negative for Vale, positive for steelmakers).
The story is on topic but has no clear direction for the coverage (methodology notes, events, general macro).

An official filing by the company itself (material fact, market announcement, shareholder notice, press release), taken from B3's real-time feed with the document filed with the CVM. Not press coverage.
Sector of the story: Steel & Mining, Pulp & Paper, or Natural Resources when it is macro or cross-sector.

S&P Platts and Fastmarkets (subscription terminals, read with our credentials), Brazilian press (Valor, Folha, Estadão, InfoMoney, Exame…), sector publications (Mining.com, GMK Center, SteelRadar, Portal Celulose, Papnews…), Reuters and Chinese sources (SCMP, Global Times).

sections.title: Market Pulse
sections.intro: The panel on the home page with the tone of the day's news and the expected opening gap.

items.desc: Balance of positive vs negative takes on the news published today. It describes the newsflow; it is not a forecast.
What moved abroad while Brazil slept: iron ore in Singapore, Chinese steel, ADRs in pre-market, FX, US futures — grouped by theme with the headline that explains each driver.

Expected opening move of each covered stock given the overnight drivers, with an 80% band. The model publishes a name only when its measured out-of-sample accuracy (IC) is above our threshold; the scoreboard shows the realised hit rate.
Correlation between predicted and realised gaps on days the model did not see. Above ~0.5 is strong; the panel shows it per company.

sections.title: Stock Guide
sections.intro: Comp table, global peers and sensitivity tables.

items.desc: EV/EBITDA, P/E, P/CE, dividend yield and upside are recalculated with the latest share price on top of our published estimates (2026E/2027E). Net debt/EBITDA does not depend on price.
Our 12-month target and the distance from the current price. Rating: OP outperform, MP market perform, UP underperform.
The 9×9 grids published in the analyst's own model (e.g., iron ore × FX for Vale): EBITDA, EV/EBITDA, FCF and FCF yield. The orange marker shows where today's spot price sits on the grid.
International comparables (BHP, Rio Tinto, ArcelorMittal, Nucor, Stora Enso…) on the same multiples.

sections.title: Market Watch
sections.intro: Public B3 and CVM data on positioning, capital returns and insiders.

items.desc: Total open securities-lending position of a ticker (registered + electronic loans). The closest public proxy for the short position in Brazil.
Shares on loan ÷ shares in circulation of the SAME class: a PN ticker is measured against the PN float, units against unit-equivalents (1 ON + 4 PN), BDRs against total shares.
Annualised fee paid to borrow the stock, weighted by the day's registered loans. Rising rates with rising loans = shorts crowding in; B3 repeats the last rate on days with no trades.
Programs approved by the board: authorised quantity, share of the float at approval, deadline and appointed brokers. The CVM does not publish execution; that comes from the companies.
Purchases and sales by the controlling shareholder, board, officers, fiscal council and committees (and related persons), with price, volume and broker.
Every document the company files: material facts, announcements, minutes, presentations, statements. 'Newsworthy' keeps the ones that carry news.

sections.title: Macro & FX
sections.intro: Rates and currencies used across the dashboard.

items.term: USD/BRL, USD/CNY, USD/CLP, USD/MXN, USD/AUD, USD/CAD, USD/EUR
items.desc: Exchange rates of Brazil, China (iron ore and steel demand), Chile and Mexico (CMPC, Copec, Grupo México trade in local currency) and the currencies of competing commodity exporters.
Policy rate, interbank rate, 12-month inflation and quarterly GDP.
Global risk-free reference; moves with gold and with emerging-market flows.
